0.long_answer: Osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis (OSCS) is characterized by specific skeletal changes and may sometimes be accompanied by other developmental anomalies. One of the overlapping features seen in the differential diagnosis of OSCS and the other disorders mentioned is the presence of congenital heart defects. Holt–Oram syndrome is well known for its cardiac septal anomalies (heart–hand syndrome), and similarly, both Noonan syndrome and Alagille syndrome are frequently associated with congenital cardiovascular malformations. Thus, the symptom that OSCS shares with these syndromes is congenital heart defects.
